answer: A registry can resist fake identities by requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake behind a single verifiable credential, like an opal seal that cannot be split across copies. Peers mirror that seal in their own attestations, so a duplicate identity shows up as the same seal claimed twice and both copies lose their stake. A sybil farm must then fund every fake separately, and each detected duplicate creates a ripple of revoked trust that burns the attacker's whole stake pool instead of just one account.
